text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a practice where developers regularly add their code changes to a shared repository. Every time someone submits new code, an automated build starts immediately. The system also runs tests to check that everything works correctly. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become serious problems. A CI pipeline usually includes several steps, such as building the software, running automated tests, and reporting results. When a problem appears, the team can fix it quickly. CI saves time and improves code quality. Many modern software teams use CI because it makes development faster and more reliable.
